title: Contextual tiling and sorting discovery for lazy grid
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a compact, contextual tiling pattern for the virtualized table component that improves discoverability of sorting and filtering for high-cardinality datasets. The goal is to reduce cognitive load when users work with very large, lazy-loaded grids by surfacing lightweight controls inline, progressively revealing advanced controls, and preserving keyboard-first resizing and accessibility semantics. This ticket focuses on UX patterns and high-fidelity specs for engineering handoff (no implementation work in this ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Detailed interaction spec for inline sort affordance that works with virtualization (hover, focus, persistent state)
Wireframes showing three density presets (compact, default, comfortable) and how tiling adapts to each
Accessible keyboard flows for column resize, multi-column sort, and filter chip keyboard management documented
A11y checklist satisfied: screen reader labels, announce changes for dynamic column reflow, focus management for progressive reveal
Edge cases: empty state, partially loaded pages, fallback when virtualization skips header re-measurement addressed
design_notes: We observed support tickets where users missed filter controls in wide tables; solution should surface primary filter controls inline to the column header with a single-icon compact mode.
Avoid persistent mega-toolbar: prefer contextual disclosure to keep primary chrome minimal for data-dense views.
Column resize must be keyboard-first: arrow increments + modifier for large jumps, and persistent width preview shown in a11y hint region.
When virtualization unloads offscreen columns, maintain virtual index-to-visual mapping so sorting and pinned columns do not jump unexpectedly.
Density presets will adjust font-size, padding, and column-gutter rhythm; include token map for spacing and hit-target changes.
design_decisions: Use a three-tier filter discovery pattern: icon-only inline opener -> compact overlay for simple filters -> full filter panel for complex queries.
Sorting will support click (single-column toggle asc/desc/none) + shift-click for multi-column compound sorting; UI shows sort chips in header when active.
Column snapping removed; instead offer soft snap with 8px magnet to avoid jarring jumps when resizing under virtualization.
Prefer CSS variable tokens for density so engineering can switch modes without remounting component trees.
